analyzed_vuln.description: Heap out-of-bounds read is caused by missing bounds validation before 16-bit field extraction in DNS answer parsing. In search_valid_dns(), after getNameLength() advances x, the code calls rsp_type = get16(&x, flow->packet.payload) at line ~171 without ensuring x+1 is within payload_packet_len. get16() blindly dereferences *(u_int16_t*)&payload[*i], so a crafted/truncated DNS response can make x point at/near end of payload and trigger a 2-byte OOB read. Crash manifests in get16(), but root cause is caller-side insufficient length checks in search_valid_dns().
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Via fuzz_process_packet, attacker-controlled packet bytes are parsed as TCP/UDP DNS (ports 53/5355 and minimum header-length gate passed). Packet must drive execution into DNS reply path with num_answers>0 and satisfy earlier loose checks ((x+6) check before name parsing, then getNameLength returning nonzero) while leaving fewer than 2 bytes available at x before rsp_type read. This truncated/malformed answer record causes get16() to read past heap buffer.
